subject: Intermittent stream stutter impacting chat UI — temporary mitigations & runbook
messages:
From: Claire Dunne <support@novasolutions.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent chat stream stutter observed today

Hi Dylan / Laura,

We started seeing periodic "stutter" in our customer-facing chat widget this morning between 09:30-11:10 UTC. The UI shows tokens arriving in small bursts and then pausing for ~2-6s before resuming — happens most frequently when concurrency spikes (15+ users).

What we've observed:
- Affected endpoint: streaming chat /v1/stream/chat
- Token arrival pattern: burst -> pause -> burst (repeat)
- Happened during our morning load test and a handful of real sessions

We've attached a client-side trace and a screenshot. Can you confirm if there were any infra events in us-west-2 around that window? Any immediate workarounds you recommend while your team investigates?

Thanks — Claire
Claire Dunne
Senior SRE, Nova Solutions
Attachments: stream_trace_20270327.json, screenshot_chat_stutter.png
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dunne <support@novasolutions.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent chat stream stutter observed today

Hi Claire — thanks for the quick report and attachments. We're looking into telemetry for the 09:30-11:10 UTC window. Initial checks show a transient increase in request fan-out at edge nodes in us-west-2 during that time; engineering is validating whether that aligns with our batching/kvm flush cadence.

Short-term mitigations you can try immediately (client side, no infra change required):
1) Fall back to non-streaming generation for critical flows: POST /v1/generate (returns full response at once). This avoids token-by-token delivery issues until we confirm root cause.
2) Reduce max_tokens to 256 for the high-concurrency cohort — lower token budgets reduce buffer pressure.
3) Use smaller streaming chunk sizes where possible (client-side accumulation window 150-300ms) to smooth arrival pattern.
4) Enable client-side exponential backoff on 502/503 and a small jitter for retries (recommended policy: base 150ms * 2^n, max 2s).
5) Enable prefix/KV caching in the request (if you pin system prompts) — that will reduce per-request KV loads.

If you'd prefer we can flip your routing to a Dedicated capacity pool for the next 72 hours; that will give more consistent token throughput while we root-cause the issue. I can open the ticket and coordinate procurement if you want to pursue that.

Please upload the full server-side request_id sample (x-rw-request-id header) for any session that still shows stutter — that'll let us correlate traces across the edge and runtime.

I'll loop in Eng and keep you posted by EOD PST with initial findings.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Account Engineer — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 06:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent chat stream stutter observed today

Thanks Dylan — we tried switching a small percentage of traffic to the non-streaming endpoint and lowered token budgets for the load test. The UI stutter reduced but we still see intermittent pauses under sustained bursts (20-30 concurrent streams). I've attached an additional server-side trace file (stream_trace_20270327.json) which includes x-rw-request-id values.

Two quick asks:
- Can you open an internal ticket for postmortem and link us?
- If Dedicated routing is the fastest path to stability, please propose a short-term plan and cost estimate.

Appreciate the quick triage — Claire

Summary (what we know):
- Symptom: token delivery pauses of 2-6s during high concurrency; pattern reported by Nova Solutions on 2027-03-27 09:30-11:10 UTC.
- Preliminary signal: transient edge node fan-out and batching alignment issue in us-west-2 contributing to uneven token emission.

Immediate actions (0-72 hrs):
- Engineering: full correlation of x-rw-request-id traces across edge -> runtime (RED-4521).
- Customer-facing mitigations (applied by Nova): fallback to non-streaming for critical flows; reduce max_tokens; enable client jitter/backoff.
- Short-term stability: offer Dedicated routing for 72h (provisioning within 4-6 hrs). Ben, can you provide a quick cost estimate and agree SLA for a 72-hour Dedicated allocation?
- Credits: I'll propose a 25% pro-rated credit for the affected window pending final RCA.

What we need from Nova now:
- Any remaining request_ids showing stutter (please send list).
- Confirmation if you want Dedicated routing for the trial window.

I'll run daily status updates in this thread until we close RED-4521. Thank you for the detailed traces — they're very helpful.

Best,
